title: The invoice that changed after it was paid
blurb: Finalized invoices were editable and tax timeouts issued zeros.
prompt: An auditor found a paid invoice whose line items had been edited weeks later, and a batch of invoices had been issued with zero tax during a tax-service outage. Retried finalizes also minted duplicate invoices. Review it, fix it, and prove finals are immutable and tax gates.
aiNote: The draft treats finalize as a state label rather than a lock, so updates still land on issued invoices and invalidate every downstream reconciliation, and it substitutes tax zero on timeout instead of holding, quietly under-charging in a way nobody reconciles.
testIdea: Attempt to update a finalized invoice and assert 409; time out the tax call and assert finalize holds with a marker; replay finalize and assert one invoice and one number.
followUps: Who may ever adjust a finalized invoice, and how is it represented?
How do gapless numbers survive a crash?
What does a tax breakdown need for audit?
